learn.rule: A sentence is a whole idea. It tells who or what, and what happens.
learn.ruleEs: Una oración es una idea completa. Dice quién o qué, y qué pasa.
learn.model: The bat sleeps upside down all day.
learn.notice: Who is the sentence about? What does the bat do? Both parts are there.

items.prompt: Which group of words is a whole sentence about bats?

options.text: Hanging upside down in caves.
Bats sleep in dark caves.
Because bats like the dark.

items.why: This one tells who (bats) and what happens (they sleep). The others leave out who or leave the idea unfinished.
items.whyEs: Esta dice quién (bats) y qué pasa (duermen). Las otras no dicen quién o dejan la idea sin terminar.

items.prompt: Which words are NOT a sentence yet? Think about tree frogs.

options.text: Frogs lay eggs in water.
Frogs can jump far.
The tiny green tree frog.

items.why: It names who, but it never says what the frog does. A sentence needs both parts.
items.whyEs: Dice quién, pero nunca dice qué hace la rana. Una oración necesita las dos partes.

items.prompt: Which one fixes the fragment 'Swims in the cold ocean'?

options.text: The penguin swims in the cold ocean.
Swims in the cold ocean and fast.
The penguin in the cold ocean.

items.why: Adding who (the penguin) gives the action a doer, so the idea is whole.
items.whyEs: Al agregar quién (the penguin), la acción tiene quien la hace y la idea queda completa.

items.prompt: Choose the words that make a whole sentence.
items.model: A spider spins a web to catch insects.
items.why: Spins a web is what the spider does. The other choices only describe or tell where.
items.whyEs: Spins a web es lo que hace la araña. Las otras opciones solo describen o dicen dónde.

items.prompt: Which one runs two ideas together without a joiner?

options.text: Whales breathe air, but they live in the ocean.
Whales live in the ocean.
Whales breathe air they live in the ocean.

items.why: This is a run-on: two whole ideas are squished together. Split them or add a joining word like but.
items.whyEs: Es una oración corrida: dos ideas completas están pegadas. Sepáralas o agrega una palabra como but.

items.prompt: Check every complete sentence about animals.

options.text: Birds build nests in trees.
Under the warm sun.
A butterfly rests on a flower.
Eating sweet nectar.

items.why: The two sentences name who and tell what happens. The other two are fragments.
items.whyEs: Las dos oraciones dicen quién y qué pasa. Las otras dos son fragmentos.

write.prompt: Write one complete sentence about an animal you know.
write.promptEs: Escribe una oración completa sobre un animal que conoces.

label: I started with a capital letter
Empecé con mayúscula
I told who and what happens
Dije quién y qué pasa

write.model: Elephants use their long trunks to drink water.

familyTalk.en: At dinner, take turns saying one whole idea about a pet or an animal. Ask: who is it about, and what happens?
familyTalk.es: En la cena, túrnense para decir una idea completa sobre una mascota o un animal. Pregunten: ¿de quién se trata y qué pasa?

teacherTip.en: Write one fragment on the board and ask students to add the missing who or what happens before they type.
teacherTip.es: Escribe un fragmento en la pizarra y pide que agreguen el quién o el qué pasa que falta antes de escribir.

learn.rule: A sentence is a whole idea. If a group of words leaves you waiting, it is a fragment.
learn.ruleEs: Una oración es una idea completa. Si un grupo de palabras te deja esperando, es un fragmento.
learn.model: The librarian helps children find good books.
learn.notice: Who helps? The librarian. What does she do? Helps children find books.

items.prompt: Which one is a whole sentence about a mail carrier?

options.text: Walks down the street.
Mail carriers bring letters and packages.
The kind mail carrier on our street.

items.why: It says who (mail carriers) and what they do (bring letters and packages).
items.whyEs: Dice quién (mail carriers) y qué hacen (bring letters and packages).

items.prompt: Which words are a fragment? Look for an unfinished idea.

options.text: Police officers keep our town safe.
Our city library has many books.
After the library closes on Friday.

items.why: After starts an idea, but it never finishes. What happens after the library closes?
items.whyEs: After empieza una idea, pero no la termina. ¿Qué pasa después de que cierra la biblioteca?

items.prompt: Which sentence squeezes two ideas together without a joiner?

options.text: Teachers help students learn.
Nurses care for sick people at the clinic.
Bus drivers wake up early they drive children to school.

items.why: Bus drivers wake up early and they drive children to school are two ideas stuck together. That is a run-on.
items.whyEs: Bus drivers wake up early y they drive children to school son dos ideas pegadas. Eso es una oración corrida.

items.prompt: Choose the words that finish the sentence about the crossing guard.
items.model: The crossing guard helps children cross the street.
items.why: Helps children cross is the action. Without an action, the idea is not whole.
items.whyEs: Helps children cross es la acción. Sin una acción, la idea no está completa.

items.prompt: Fix the run-on: 'Doctors help sick people they work in hospitals.'

options.text: Doctors help sick people, they work in hospitals.
Doctors help sick people. They work in hospitals.
Doctors help sick people work in hospitals.

items.why: A period splits the two whole ideas. A comma alone is too weak, and the last one changes the meaning.
items.whyEs: El punto separa las dos ideas completas. Una coma sola no basta, y la última cambia el significado.

items.prompt: Check every complete sentence about our town.

options.text: Our town has a small park.
Many kids playing on the swings.
The park has a pond with ducks.
Near the old stone bridge.

items.why: Each right answer has who or what and a full action. The others are missing a piece.
items.whyEs: Cada respuesta correcta tiene quién o qué y una acción completa. A las otras les falta una parte.

write.prompt: Write one complete sentence about a helper in your community.
write.promptEs: Escribe una oración completa sobre una persona que ayuda en tu comunidad.

label: I started with a capital letter
Empecé con mayúscula
I told who and what happens
Dije quién y qué pasa

write.model: A firefighter drives a big red truck to emergencies.

familyTalk.en: On a walk, point to a worker you see. Say a whole sentence about the job together.
familyTalk.es: En un paseo, señalen a una persona que trabaja. Digan juntos una oración completa sobre su trabajo.

teacherTip.en: Have partners read each answer aloud and listen for whether the idea feels finished.
teacherTip.es: Pide que las parejas lean cada respuesta en voz alta y escuchen si la idea se siente terminada.

learn.rule: A sentence is a whole idea. Check for who or what, and what happens.
learn.ruleEs: Una oración es una idea completa. Busca quién o qué, y qué pasa.
learn.model: A square has four equal sides.
learn.notice: What is the sentence about? A square. What do we learn? It has four equal sides.

items.prompt: Which group of words is a whole sentence about a triangle?

options.text: Three straight sides and three corners.
The triangle on the page.
A triangle has three straight sides.

items.why: It names the shape and tells a fact about it. The others do not finish an idea.
items.whyEs: Nombra la figura y dice un dato sobre ella. Las otras no terminan una idea.

items.prompt: Which one is a fragment? Think about hexagons.

options.text: When you count the sides of a hexagon.
A hexagon has six sides.
Honeycomb cells have six sides.

items.why: The word when starts an idea, but we still do not know what happens. It needs more.
items.whyEs: La palabra when empieza una idea, pero todavía no sabemos qué pasa. Le falta más.

items.prompt: Which sentence about a cube is a run-on?

options.text: A cube has six flat faces.
A cube has six flat faces it has eight corners.
A cube has eight corners.

items.why: Two whole ideas run together with no stop or joiner. Use a period or and.
items.whyEs: Dos ideas completas están pegadas sin punto ni palabra de unión. Usa un punto o and.

items.prompt: Pick the words that make a whole sentence about a pentagon.
items.model: A pentagon has five straight sides.
items.why: Has is a verb, so it tells what the pentagon does or is. The other two only describe.
items.whyEs: Has es un verbo, así que dice qué es o qué tiene el pentágono. Las otras solo describen.

items.prompt: Which words turn 'Counting the corners of the cube' into a sentence?

options.text: Counting the corners of the cube, and the faces.
Nia is counting the corners of the cube.
Counting the corners of the cube slowly.

items.why: Adding Nia is gives the action a doer and a helping verb, so the idea is complete.
items.whyEs: Al agregar Nia is, la acción tiene quien la hace y un verbo auxiliar, y la idea queda completa.

items.prompt: Check every complete sentence about shapes.

options.text: A circle rolls easily.
Round like a ball.
The shapes on the shelf.
A triangle has three corners.

items.why: Both right answers name a shape and tell what it does or has.
items.whyEs: Las dos respuestas correctas nombran una figura y dicen qué hace o qué tiene.

write.prompt: Write one complete sentence about a shape you see in your classroom.
write.promptEs: Escribe una oración completa sobre una figura que ves en tu salón.

label: I started with a capital letter
Empecé con mayúscula
I told what the shape is or does
Dije qué es o qué hace la figura

write.model: The clock on our wall is a circle.

familyTalk.en: Find a shape at home, like a plate or a window. Say one whole sentence about it.
familyTalk.es: Busquen una figura en casa, como un plato o una ventana. Digan una oración completa sobre ella.

teacherTip.en: Ask students to hold up a thumb when they hear a whole idea and to wait when the idea is unfinished.
teacherTip.es: Pide que levanten el pulgar cuando escuchen una idea completa y que esperen si la idea no está terminada.
